events.title: The death of Blessed John Duns Scotus
events.shortBlurb: The Subtle Doctor, who had forged the classic defense of Our Lady's Immaculate Conception, died suddenly at Cologne…
body: Born about 1266 at Duns in the Scottish Borders, John Duns Scotus entered the Friars Minor and studied and taught at Oxford, Paris, and Cologne. The keenness of his mind won him the title Doctor Subtilis, the Subtle Doctor, and later ages ranked him with Thomas Aquinas, Bonaventure, and William of Ockham among the great theologians of the medieval schools.

His most celebrated achievement was the classic defense of the Immaculate Conception. Where others feared it derogated from Christ's universal redemption, Scotus argued that the most perfect Redeemer would preserve his Mother from original sin from the first instant of her being — a redemption more excellent, not less. The maxim later attached to his school, "potuit, decuit, ergo fecit" (God could do it, it was fitting, therefore he did it), summed up the case that Pius IX would define as dogma in 1854.

Transferred to the Franciscan studium at Cologne about 1307, he died there unexpectedly on 8 November 1308 and was buried in the Minorite church. His sarcophagus bears the verse "Scotia me genuit, Anglia me suscepit, Gallia me docuit, Colonia me tenet." Pope John Paul II beatified him in 1993.
